extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, appellants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), requests for rehearing, examiner actions after Board decisions, reopening prosecution, RCEs, and withdrawal/dismissal of appeals under the MPEP and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing timing and single-request limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the date of the original Board decision; no request for rehearing from a decision on rehearing will be permitted unless the rehearing decision so modified the original decision as to become, in effect, a new decision and the Board states a second request would be permitted. (37 CFR 41.52(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period can only be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) in ex parte reexamination proceedings. The date of the decision is the mailing/notification date on form PTOL-90. The decision on rehearing is final for purposes of judicial review except as specifically noted in the decision on rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement for requests for rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many requests are merely reargument of positions; the rule limits rehearing requests to points of law or fact the appellant believes the Board overlooked or misapprehended. Arguments not previously raised and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in the rehearing request except as allowed by the specific exceptions (see related metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted new material in a rehearing request (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in a rehearing request, except that appellant may present: (A) new argument(s) based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court; (B) new argument(s) responding to a new ground of rejection designated pursuant to 37 CFR 41.50(b); and (C) new argument(s) that the Board's decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection. (37 CFR 41.52(a)(2)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on a recent decision, a remand to the examiner to respond may be appropriate. These exceptions are narrowly construed; rehearing is typically limited to the written record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing is on the written record only (no entitlement to oral hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'rehearing' in 37 CFR 41.52 refers to rehearing on the written record and should not be interpreted as an entitlement to an oral hearing on the request for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the normal practice of the Board to grant another oral hearing on a rehearing request. (Citations: Ex parte Argoudelis and supporting MPEP text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rehearing decision on finality and judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on a request for rehearing incorporates the earlier opinion except for portions specifically withdrawn on rehearing and is final for purposes of judicial review, except when noted otherwise in the rehearing decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for filing a request for rehearing runs from the date of the Board decision making the original affirmance final; the mailing/notification date on PTOL-90 is controlling. See MPEP §§ 1214.03 and 1216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 37 CFR 41.50(b) new grounds by appellant (two paths)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board enters a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b), the appellant may (1) proceed before the examiner under 41.50(b)(1) by amending the claims and/or submitting new evidence (which reopens prosecution before the examiner), or (2) elect to file a request for rehearing under 41.50(b)(2), which waives further prosecution before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant presents only arguments against the new ground without amendment/evidence, jurisdiction should remain with the Board (i.e., the matter is best handled by the Board). If appellant chooses to reopen prosecution (amend/submit evidence), prosecution is reopened and the case returns to the examiner. If the 41.50(b) rejection is not overcome, a second appeal may be filed but must be limited to the 41.50(b) rejection and not include the affirmed rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on arguments/evidence in rehearing replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised and evidence not previously relied upon pursuant to §§ 41.37, 41.41, or 41.47 are not permitted in the request for rehearing except as specifically permitted (recent decisions, responses to new grounds, or alleged undesignated new grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies to both appellants and examiners when making rehearing requests; any party invoking a recent decision should be prepared for a possible remand to the examiner to address the new argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing procedural timeline interplay with court review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely request for rehearing is filed, the time for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencing a civil action expires 63 days after the decision on the rehearing request. More generally, the time to seek court review under 37 CFR 90.3 is 63 days (plus any granted extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rehearing is timely filed before the Board, the 63-day appellate clock runs from the Board's decision on rehearing or reconsideration. See MPEP §§ 1214.03 and 1216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action after complete reversal of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reversal of the examiner's rejection brings the case up for immediate action by the examiner; if the reversal does not place the application in condition for allowance, examiner should follow guidance in MPEP § 1214.06 for appropriate actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should bring the prior art search up-to-date but should never treat a reversal as authorization to conduct a fresh search to uncover other/better references. If a new examiner believes the prior art search is incomplete (e.g., due to new claim interpretation), the issue should be raised with the SPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner proposing new rejection after Board reversal requires authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner proposes a new rejection of appealed claims (for reasons other than 37 CFR 1.114 or 41.50), the examiner must submit the matter to the Technology Center (TC) Director or Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198 for entering the new rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval by TC/CRU Director is placed on the action reopening prosecution. Examiner requests for rehearing of the Board decision must be approved by the TC/CRU Director and forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval before mailing. The request should normally set a 2-month period for appellant reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when Board sustains examiner in whole/part — no claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: When no claims stand allowed after Board decision and the period for seeking court review expires, proceedings are terminated; a Notice of Abandonment should be prepared and mailed. If provisional or double patenting rejections exist, applicant may file a terminal disclaimer prior to the expiration to attempt to overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims objected to as allowable except for dependency are treated as rejected unless rewritten in independent form within the period for seeking review. Examiner options when dependent claim(s) become allowable only after reversal of independent claims: (1) Convert dependent claim(s) into independent form by examiner’s amendment, cancel affirmed claims, and issue; or (2) set a 2-month time limit for applicant to rewrite dependent claim(s) in independent form (extensions under 1.136 available). Use provided form paragraphs (e.g., ¶12.291).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when some claims stand allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims stand allowed after Board decision, the examiner issues the application or reexamination certificate on the allowed claims; canceled rejected claims need not be cancelled by applicant as examiner may cancel by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowed claims depend on other claims that were affirmed, examiner may convert dependent claims to independent form or set a 2-month period for applicant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form; if formal matters remain, send a shortened-period letter (form ¶12.297) requiring correction within two months to avoid abandonment (extensions under 1.136 available, but cannot extend beyond 6-month statutory maximum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-elected claims and provisional double patenting after Board reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision reverses rejections of generic claims in an application containing non-elected species, pending claims drawn to non-elected species must be acted upon (consider rejoinder) unless the examiner reopens prosecution and determines the election remains appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection was not reached by the Board and the reference application has issued as a patent, the provisional rejection should be reissued as a non-provisional rejection and a terminal disclaimer required. If the reference application was abandoned or never matured and the provisional DPT rejection is the only remaining rejection, the examiner should withdraw the provisional rejection. See MPEP § 804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after final Board decision (RCE and 1.198 petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened after a final Board decision except under 37 CFR 1.114 (RCE), 37 CFR 41.50 with Director authority, or by petition under 37 CFR 1.198 with Director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed with an RCE (and the appropriate fee) will be entered and prosecution reopened; if an amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance, examiner should recommend entry even without an RCE, with supervisory concurrence. If an amendment cannot be entered, the examiner must notify appellant of the reason; the refusal must not be arbitrary or capricious. Use form ¶12.298 when refusing entry. Petitions under 1.198 to reopen are decided by the TC Director and are ordinarily granted only in limited categories (A) decision suggests claims could be made allowable by adding disclosed limitation/curing defect, (B) decision indicates missing evidence that exists and can be offered, or (C) decision based on a rule/practice/law/judicial precedent since rescinded/repealed/overruled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director petitions and remand procedures after petition grant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen prosecution is granted by the Director, steps may be taken to request the court to remand the case to the USPTO or, in a 35 U.S.C. 145 civil action, to obtain dismissal without prejudice so the proposed amendments/evidence/arguments can be entered for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remanded, the proposals will be entered of record and further action will be taken by the Board in the first instance or by the examiner as appropriate. Such petitions are ordinarily not entertained after the Director's brief is filed in 35 U.S.C. 141 cases or after trial in 35 U.S.C. 145 cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal and interplay with RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal is withdrawn after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired, the application is considered abandoned as of the withdrawal date unless there are allowed claims. The filing of an RCE prior to a Board decision reopens prosecution and is treated as a withdrawal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filed without the appropriate fee or a submission in an application with no allowed claims will result in abandonment. To avoid abandonment, an RCE must comply with 37 CFR 1.114 (include the fee and a statement/transmittal identifying any incorporated material as required). If a brief was filed and appellant withdraws prior to transfer of jurisdiction to the Board, the application is returned to the examiner; if after transfer, dismissal is handled by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-withdrawal effect and examiner handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon withdrawal of an appeal, an application with no allowed claims is abandoned and a Notice of Abandonment should be mailed. Claims that were allowable only because of dependency from rejected claims are treated as rejected unless rewritten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request reopening in certain situations (e.g., reply addressing a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer within two months) as outlined in MPEP § 1215.01. Applicants should promptly inform the Clerk of the Board if they refile or abandon a continuation to avoid the Board issuing decisions on applications already refiled.
